socraticQuestions.prompt: What is Bonferroni's Principle and why does it matter in data mining?
socraticQuestions.answer: It states that if you search many combinations, you will find spurious patterns by chance; you must account for the search space when judging significance.
socraticQuestions.hint: Searching many combinations creates false discoveries.

socraticQuestions.prompt: Why does the terrorist-hunting example produce so many suspicious pairs?
socraticQuestions.answer: Because the number of person-pairs and day-pairs is enormous, so even tiny per-pair probabilities yield many expected coincidences.
socraticQuestions.hint: Multiply large counts by small probabilities.

slides.title: Theorem: No false negatives

extraction.text:
Theorem: No false negatives
• If there is an itemset S  that is frequent in full data, but not
frequent in the sample (false negative), then the negative
border contains at least one itemset that is frequent in the
whole (algorithm does not terminate)
Proof by contradiction:
• Suppose not.  i.e.
1. There is an itemset S  frequent in the full data but not
frequent in the sample, and
2. Nothing in the negative border is frequent in the full data
• Let T  be a smallest subset of S that is not frequent in the
sample (every subset of T is frequent in the sample)

T  is frequent in the whole (subset of frequent set S).

T  is in the negative border (contradiction)
